main.title: Rita Levi-Montalcini wins the Nobel Prize
main.summary: In 1986, Rita Levi-Montalcini and Stanley Cohen shared the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for their discoveries of growth factors.

cards.heading: Rita Levi-Montalcini wins the Nobel Prize
cards.text:
Rita Levi-Montalcini and Stanley Cohen shared the 1986 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for their discoveries of growth factors, including nerve growth factor. Their work brought international recognition to the Italian neurobiologist, born in 1909.

Levi-Montalcini became an Italian senator for life in 2001 in recognition of her scientific contribution and served until her death in 2012. On April 22, 2009, she became the first Nobel laureate to reach the age of one hundred, celebrated at Rome's City Hall.

main.title: Watchmen #1
main.summary: DC began publishing Watchmen in 1986, with Alan Moore writing, Dave Gibbons drawing and John Higgins colouring its twelve-part story.

cards.heading: Watchmen #1
cards.text: DC began publishing Watchmen in 1986, with Alan Moore writing, Dave Gibbons drawing and John Higgins colouring its twelve-part story. It imagines a world where costumed heroes have altered American history and the United States approaches war with the Soviet Union. Most vigilantes are retired, outlawed or employed by the government. Moore originally proposed using characters acquired from Charlton Comics, but the team created new ones to give the story freedom over their fates. Their powers, compromises and political roles allowed the series to examine the superhero idea through contemporary anxieties.

main.title: European operators agree on GSM
main.summary: A September 1987 agreement committed European operators to developing and deploying a shared digital mobile network standard.

cards.heading: An agreement for mobile communication
cards.text:
In September 1987, European operators signed a memorandum in Copenhagen committing them to a common digital cellular system. The agreement brought together fifteen operators from thirteen countries around the development and deployment of GSM, helping create a shared market for networks and compatible equipment.

GSM initially focused on digital voice calls using time-division multiple access. Later extensions added data services through GPRS and EDGE. Cooperation over compatible networks also supported international roaming, allowing subscribers to use their phones beyond their home country.

main.title: The Joshua Tree
main.summary: U2 released The Joshua Tree on 9 March 1987, with Daniel Lanois and Brian Eno producing.

cards.heading: The Joshua Tree
cards.text: U2 released The Joshua Tree on 9 March 1987, with Daniel Lanois and Brian Eno producing. The band brought American and Irish roots music into direct song structures, pairing spiritual imagery with political concerns. Experiences in the United States fed both admiration for its mythology and unease about its reality. Recording in Irish houses encouraged a relaxed working atmosphere. Events around the sessions also shaped the lyrics, including Amnesty International benefit concerts, Bono's travels in Central America and the death of roadie Greg Carroll. Those personal and public experiences run through the record together.

main.title: The Last Emperor
main.subtitle: Puyi learns the limits of power behind the palace walls
main.summary: Bernardo Bertolucci's The Last Emperor follows Puyi from his childhood enthronement in 1908 through the upheavals that end imperial rule in China. John Lone plays the adult Puyi, with Joan Chen and Peter O'Toole among the international cast. Released in 1987, the film places the scale of a historical epic around a man whose apparent power repeatedly conceals his dependence on others.

cards.heading: A child becomes emperor
cards.text: Bernardo Bertolucci's The Last Emperor follows Puyi from his childhood enthronement in 1908 through the upheavals that end imperial rule in China. John Lone plays the adult Puyi, with Joan Chen and Peter O'Toole among the international cast. Released in 1987, the film places the scale of a historical epic around a man whose apparent power repeatedly conceals his dependence on others.

cards.heading: Authority and dependence
cards.text: Inside the Forbidden City, ritual gives the child emperor an extraordinary status while restricting what he can see and do. As Puyi grows older, the world beyond its walls changes faster than the court around him. His attempts to regain authority later make him useful to other political interests. The film returns to his imprisonment and questioning, allowing different stages of his life to challenge the explanations he has learned to give for his choices.

cards.heading: The changing rooms of a life
cards.text: Vittorio Storaro's photography and Ferdinando Scarfiotti's production design distinguish the enclosed splendour of the palace from the environments Puyi later inhabits. The crowd that once bows before a child and the restrictions surrounding the adult ruler express different forms of control. Music by Ryuichi Sakamoto, David Byrne and Cong Su adds further changes of atmosphere. The film won all nine Academy Awards for which it was nominated, including best picture and Bertolucci's direction.

main.title: Akira
main.summary: Akira is Katsuhiro Otomo's 1988 animated cyberpunk film, following Kaneda and Tetsuo through a crisis in the futuristic city of Neo-Tokyo.

cards.heading: Akira
cards.text:
Akira is a 1988 Japanese animated cyberpunk action thriller film directed by Katsuhiro Otomo, produced by Ryōhei Suzuki and Shunzō Katō, and written by Otomo and Izo Hashimoto, based on Otomo's 1982 manga Akira. Set in a dystopian 2019, it follows Shōtarō Kaneda, the leader of a biker gang whose childhood friend, Tetsuo Shima, acquires powerful telekinetic abilities after colliding with a child esper in a motorcycle accident, eventually threatening an entire military complex in the sprawling futuristic metropolis of Neo-Tokyo.

While most of the character designs and settings were adapted from the manga, the plot differs considerably and does not include much of the latter half of the manga, which continued publication for two years after the film's release. The soundtrack, which draws heavily from traditional Indonesian gamelan and Japanese noh music, was composed by Shōji Yamashiro and performed by Geinoh Yamashirogumi.

main.title: My Neighbor Totoro
main.summary: My Neighbor Totoro is a 1988 Japanese animated fantasy film written and directed by Hayao Miyazaki and animated by Studio Ghibli for Tokuma Shoten.

cards.heading: My Neighbor Totoro
cards.text:
My Neighbor Totoro is a 1988 Japanese animated fantasy film written and directed by Hayao Miyazaki and animated by Studio Ghibli for Tokuma Shoten. It stars the voices of Noriko Hidaka, Chika Sakamoto and Hitoshi Takagi, and focuses on two young sisters who, after moving with their father to the countryside, experience interactions with friendly wood spirits in postwar Japan.

The film explores themes such as animism, Shinto symbology, environmentalism, childhood and the joys of rural living. My Neighbor Totoro received worldwide critical acclaim, and grossed over $41 million worldwide at the box office; the film also grossed significantly more from home video sales and merchandise.

My Neighbor Totoro received numerous awards, including the Animage Anime Grand Prix prize, the Mainichi Film Award, and Kinema Junpo Award for Best Film in 1988. It also received the Special Award at the Blue Ribbon Awards in the same year.

main.title: Cinema Paradiso
main.subtitle: A projection booth becomes a school for a young film lover
main.summary: Giuseppe Tornatore's Cinema Paradiso follows Salvatore, a successful director looking back on his childhood friendship with a cinema projectionist. Released in Italy in 1988 under the title Nuovo Cinema Paradiso, the film gives that friendship a home in a Sicilian town's picture house. Philippe Noiret plays Alfredo, the man whose working life introduces a boy to the machinery and pleasures of cinema.

cards.heading: A friendship in the projection booth
cards.text: Giuseppe Tornatore's Cinema Paradiso follows Salvatore, a successful director looking back on his childhood friendship with a cinema projectionist. Released in Italy in 1988 under the title Nuovo Cinema Paradiso, the film gives that friendship a home in a Sicilian town's picture house. Philippe Noiret plays Alfredo, the man whose working life introduces a boy to the machinery and pleasures of cinema.

cards.heading: How a town watches films
cards.text: Young Totò is drawn to the projection booth, where reels, light and a dangerous machine turn into images for a crowded auditorium. Alfredo's instruction mixes practical knowledge with impatience and affection. Below them, the audience makes its own performance: people laugh, argue and return to familiar seats. The local priest's demands to remove screen kisses show how the films are altered before the town sees them. Cinema is both a shared gathering and something controlled by the people who run it.

cards.heading: Returning to the screen
cards.text: The adult Salvatore's return makes the building, the friendship and his departure part of the same recollection. Ennio Morricone's score gives that passage through time a strong melodic continuity. The film's final gift draws together the material work of handling film and the feelings its images preserve. Its international recognition included the Cannes Grand Prix and the foreign-language Oscar, taking a story rooted in one small cinema to audiences far beyond that town.

main.title: Tiananmen Square protests and massacre
main.summary: Students and workers gathered in Beijing's Tiananmen Square from April 1989, initially following the death of reform-minded Communist Party leader Hu Yaobang.

cards.heading: Tiananmen Square protests and massacre
cards.text: Students and workers gathered in Beijing's Tiananmen Square from April 1989, initially following the death of reform-minded Communist Party leader Hu Yaobang. Their demands reflected concerns about corruption, inflation and restrictions on political participation during rapid economic change. Weeks of demonstrations and unsuccessful negotiations followed. The government declared martial law in late May. On the night of 3 June, troops advanced to occupy the square, violently suppressing the movement. The protests and massacre became known internationally through the name Tiananmen and in China as the June Fourth Incident.

main.title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
main.summary: The Berlin Wall fell on 9 November 1989 during the Peaceful Revolution, marking the beginning of the destruction of the figurative Iron Curtain, as East Berlin transit restrictions were overwhelmed and discarded.

cards.heading: Fall of the Berlin Wall
cards.text: The Berlin Wall fell on 9 November 1989 during the Peaceful Revolution, marking the beginning of the destruction of the figurative Iron Curtain, as East Berlin transit restrictions were overwhelmed and discarded. Sections of the wall were breached, and planned deconstruction began the following June. It was one of the series of events that started the fall of communism in Central and Eastern Europe. The fall of the inner German border took place shortly afterward. An end to the Cold War was declared at the Malta Summit in early December, and German reunification took place in October the following year.
